html:
SMTO-GWT-0083 — The Gateway stopped a job because its access changed

GUID: 44c878b5-fe79-5743-8699-f7c59bbb4488
Slug: gateway-authorization-changed
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gateway

What happened

  • Between accepting the job and starting it, the Gateway's permission for SMTO changed or the job was stopped. The Gateway did not start it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask whoever manages the Gateway whether they just reset its pairing with SMTO or changed which workspace it may use. Such a change cancels the permission jobs were accepted under, so the Gateway refuses to start them.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection for this Gateway. This shows whether SMTO and the Gateway are still paired under the Gateway's current permission.
  3. Look at the Task in the conversation. If you or someone else stopped it, you don't need to do anything else. A stop request also prevents the job from starting, and that is expected.
  4. If you still want the work done, send the request again as a new message. The refused job never started, so new work under current permission is safe.

What success looks like

  • The new request starts on the Gateway and the Task shows it running or finished.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway. Don't delete the Task or its history; it shows the job was not started.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway's dispatch fence refused to launch the job because its pairing authorization revision or workspace access changed after acceptance, the job was not admitted, or it was cancelled before launch.

What this means

  • The dispatch fence detected a changed authorization revision, non-admitted work or cancellation before launch; a concurrent cancellation can also stop dispatch after intent is durable. The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.

Why this can happen

  • The dispatch fence detected a changed authorization revision, non-admitted work or cancellation before launch; a concurrent cancellation can also stop dispatch after intent is durable.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the job's captured/current authorization revision, admission state and cancellation state; distinguish revoked authorization from user cancellation.

How to fix it

  • Check the job record in Technical details: an authorization_revision mismatch means the Gateway's pairing was reset or re-paired (or workspace access changed) after the job was accepted; the record is marked failed_to_start, executed=false. A cancellation or non-admitted state means it was stopped first. Confirm the original job is settled, re-establish pairing if needed, then submit new work under the current authorization; do not delete the job record.
  • Inspect the original job's authorization, admission and cancellation receipt. Request new work only under current authority after settling the existing identity.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm current state and correct the reported condition before requesting another attempt. Do not replay work with an unknown outcome.

How to verify the fix

  • The original job is settled as unstarted when proven, and any new work receives current valid admission.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained evidence or retry an operation whose effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
